OurChang1957: How patterns of family living have changed from the 1880s to the 1950s, shown in dramatized sequences.

rv: An excellent review of family life and gender roles of the times. Having been born in 1956, I was raised in this manner. However, I have yet to see many men helping with the housework. I am female, and a full time carpenter. I also cook, clean, wash, etc. This film is very valuable, and in very good condition. I recommend it to everyone.

As a college/university professor I highly recommend this video if for no other reason than the cultural and historical authenticity of information provided. It doesn't get more authentic and there is in fact a wealth of information touching upon various themes about the social changes affecting not only the Family as a cultural unit but equally the roles of men, women, grandparents, and children. Remember, this video is only 55 years old yet it discusses issues that are still being debated today! Take it for what it is and enjoy it!
I would recommend this to all mature people interested in history and edutainment
Obviously that doesn't include immature casual racists like Mekoja12.
Carefully Stated...Very Matter Of Fact "Impartial" for sure

Illustrates quite accurately and objectively, the differences between farm and urban family life; and that between the late 19th century and the mid twentieth century. Shows clearly and accurately the evolutionary differences between the two during that time span. It even addresses Christian religious practices and how that changed during that period (that and the nuclear family thing would change much more drastically in the next 50 years - a subject for a movie 40 years after this). I noticed that every word and phrase in the narrative was carefully chosen - all for accuracy's sake…
